{{Short description|90th season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 2021 National Hurling League |image = |dates = 8 May – 24 July 2021 |teams = 32 |team1 = Galway / Kilkenny |captain1 = [[Pádraic Mannion]] / [[Adrian Mullen]] |manager1 = [[Shane O'Neill (Limerick hurler)|Shane O'Neill]] / [[Brian Cody]] |titles = 11th and 19th |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |twoa = Offaly |twob = Kildare |threea = Sligo |threeb = Louth |previous = [[2020 National Hurling League|2020]] |next = [[2022 National Hurling League|2022]] }} The '''2021 National Hurling League''' was the 90th season of the [[National Hurling League]] for [[county team]]s.{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40067163.html|title=Antrim earn crack at Division 1 as Kerry fall short|date=October 18, 2020|website=Irish Examiner}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40050821.html|title=Allianz Leagues 2021 set for revised, shorter format|date=September 17, 2020|website=Irish Examiner}} The English county teams (London, Warwickshire and Lancashire) did not compete due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] travel restrictions.{{Cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/intercounty-gaa-and-national-leagues-return-all-you-need-to-know-guide-1.4380159|title=Intercounty GAA and National Leagues return: All you need to know guide|first=Eamon|last=Donoghue|newspaper=The Irish Times}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sport/gaa/league-structures-in-line-for-major-overhaul-in-2021-39606358.html|title=League structures in line for major overhaul in 2021|newspaper=Belfasttelegraph |via=www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk}} In February 2021 it was announced that the league would be delayed due to the [[impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on Gaelic games]] and that cancelling it would be a last resort. The league began on 8 May 2021.{{Cite web |url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/0319/1204925-gaa-play-the-waiting-game-on-april-return-to-action/|title=GAA play the waiting game on April return to action|first=Damian|last=Lawlor|date=March 19, 2021|via=www.rte.ie}}{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/0408/1208626-gaa-roadmap-set-out-with-first-games-a-month-away/|title=GAA roadmap set out with first games a month away|date=8 April 2021|work=RTE Sport|accessdate= 9 April 2021}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/gaa-2021-roadmap-5403856-Apr2021/|title=GAA unveils 2021 roadmap with leagues starting in May and All-Ireland finals in August|first=Kevin|last=O'Brien|website=The42|date=8 April 2021 }} [[Eir Sport]] and [[RTÉ]] provided live TV coverage of the league on Saturday nights. [[TG4]] broadcast Sunday afternoon games. The highlights programmes were [[RTÉ2]]'s ''League Sunday'' on Sunday evenings, and TG4's ''GAA 2021'' on Monday evenings.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/hurling-tv-coverage-this-weekend-5427716-May2021/|title=Five hurling matches live on TV this weekend as inter-county GAA action returns|date=4 May 2021|work=The 42|accessdate= 5 May 2021}} {{GG|Galway|hurling}} and {{GG|Kilkenny|hurling}} were the joint winners. {{TOC Limit|3}} ==Format== '''League structure''' Thirty-two teams competed in the 2021 National Hurling League – * twelve teams organised in two six-team groups of approximately equal strength in Division 1 * six teams in Division 2A * five teams in Divisions 2B and 3A * four teams in Division 3B. All thirty-two county teams from Ireland took part. [[London GAA|London]], [[Lancashire GAA|Lancashire]] and Warwickshire did not take part; they retained their division placings (2B, 3A and 3B respectively) for the [[2022 National Hurling League]]. {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" |- ! colspan=7 | Teams by Province and Division |- ! Province !! Div 1 !! Div 2A !! Div 2B !! Div 3A !! Div 3B || Total |- | [[Connacht GAA|Connacht]] || 1 || 0 || 2 || 1 || 1 || 5 |- | [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]] || 5 || 4 || 1 || 1 || 1 || 12 |- | [[Munster GAA|Munster]] ||5|| 1 || 0 || 0 || 0 || 6 |- | [[Ulster GAA|Ulster]] || 1 || 1 || 2 || 3 || 2 || 9 |- | colspan=7 | |- | Total ||12|| 6 || 5 || 5 || 4 || 32 |} Each team plays all the other teams in their division once, either home or away. Two points are awarded for a win, and one for a draw. '''Tie-breaker''' * If only two teams are level on league points, the team that won the head-to-head match is ranked ahead. If this game was a draw, score difference (total scored minus total conceded in all games) is used to rank the teams. * If three or more teams are level on league points, score difference is used to rank the teams. '''Final, promotions and relegations''' '''Division 1''' * There is no final; there will either be joint winners, or if the teams that win Divisions 1A and 1B meet in the [[2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], this will double as the NHL final.{{Cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/news/gaa-announce-revised-master-fixtures-calendar-for-2021/|title=GAA announce revised Master Fixtures Calendar for 2021|website=www.gaa.ie}} * The bottom team in each group meet in a relegation play-off, with the losers being relegated to Division 2A '''Divisions 2A, 2B and 3A''' * The first-placed team is the division champion and is promoted * The bottom team is relegated '''Division 3B''' * The first-placed team is the Division 3B champion and is promoted to Division 3A ==Division 1== {{Location map+ | Ireland | AlternativeMap = Island of Ireland location map.svg | width = 350 | caption = Locations of the 2021 NHL Division 1 teams.
